# The lead's brief for step 2.111

Written by the lead on 2026-11-17 for the session that builds this step on a machine of its own (runbook, "A lane on a machine of its own"). It is that session's whole brief.

You are THE LEAD OF AREA 8 (THE BUSINESS) in the SR Leagues build, working on a cloud machine of your own, for ONE piece of work: step 2.111, "Area audit: the business". You are NOT the build's lead: that is another session (id session_01GUxQEgr89W9ggpA1toGhGY), which gave you this audit and to which you report. The repository's CLAUDE.md tells a session that has "only this repository" to read docs/build/START-HERE.md and take the build over: THAT IS NOT YOUR JOB. You never edit docs/build/STATUS.md, any stage plan, the specification or DECISIONS.md, never change product code or a test, never touch the branches `build/stage-1` or `main`, and never open a pull request. Your one output is ONE FILE, `docs/build/audits/business.md`, on your own branch.

SET-UP: from `docs/build/START-HERE.md` read only section 2a and make `.local/env.sh` as it says (you need Node only for the formatter). Set only the commits' AUTHOR from the branch's own history, without printing it: `git config author.name "$(git log -1 --format=%an origin/build/stage-1)"` and the same with `author.email` and `%ae`; change no other git setting. Make your branch: `git switch -c lane/2.111-business-audit origin/build/stage-1`. `npm ci` (for `npx prettier`).

READ: `CLAUDE.md` (who decides what; what always waits for the founder; "Talking to the founder": the audit is written in that voice, for a person who is not an engineer and often listens rather than reads); `docs/build/LEADS.md`, area 8 and how a lead audits; THE STEP'S OWN LINE, all of it: the line starting `- [ ] **2.111` in `docs/build/STAGE-2.md` (it says exactly what the report holds and its done test); the other audits in `docs/build/audits/` for their form (and `going-online.md` if it is there: its costs and vendor facts are yours to carry, marked as that audit marks them); `docs/specs/v1/PROGRESS.md`; EVERY product file of `docs/specs/v1/product/` whole; `docs/specs/v1/DECISIONS.md` whole (every row whose status is "Open", "Recommended" or "Decided for you" is yours; the change log too), and the files in `docs/specs/v1/decisions-pending/`; the legal brief (search `docs/` for "LEGAL-BRIEF"); `docs/build/STATUS.md`, the section "Needs the founder"; `docs/build/handover/founder-design-direction.md`; `docs/operations/` for what the founder is asked to do by hand.

WHO YOU ARE WRITING FOR, AND WHAT THEY NEED: one founder who runs a league (Faraj League), has a second league's tracker live (Al-Hadi), is paying for this build, and has made an AI the business and technical lead. They need to know, as someone about to RUN THIS AS A BUSINESS: (1) what is decided and built into the plans; (2) every answer that was "Decided for you", each with what it commits the business to in everyday terms, whether it is easy or costly to change later, and whether you would keep it: say plainly where you would decide differently and why; (3) what is still undecided and WHEN it starts to block (before the first online test; before the first real people have accounts; before the first league that is not the founder's own; before the first dollar is charged): prices and how money is taken, what a league is promised and what it is not, terms and privacy and children's data, support, who owns a league's data and how they leave with it, the name and the domain, insurance or a company if the spec speaks of one; (4) what it costs to run, month by month, at one league, ten and a hundred: every figure names its source in the repository or says "an estimate" and how you made it; you look nothing up on the internet and you contact no vendor; (5) the risks to the business that the build cannot remove (a child's data; a game night that fails; one person's availability; a vendor's free plan changing), each with what would lower it; (6) THE FOUNDER'S QUESTIONS, shortest first: each a question they can answer in a sentence, with your recommendation and what waits on it. You decide NOTHING for the founder and mark nothing "Agreed": you recommend.

FORM: plain everyday words; short sections with a one-line answer first; no jargon without a short explanation; a first section of at most 15 lines, "In short", that a person could hear read aloud and act on; then the sections above; a last section "What I could not check". Tables only where they truly help on a phone. The file passes `npx prettier --check docs/build/audits/business.md`.

THE DONE TEST (the line's): every open or "Decided for you" decision is in the report with what it commits to (count them in DECISIONS.md and in your report, and give both counts); each cost figure names its source or says it is an estimate; the founder's questions are listed shortest first.

COMMIT in parts as sections are finished (the message says what the part is; end each with the attribution lines your session gives you), PUSH your branch `lane/2.111-business-audit` after each part (plain pushes, never forced, no other branch; the founder allowed lane branches to be pushed on 2026-11-16). If a push is refused, do not look for a way round it: say so in your report.

WHEN YOU ARE DONE, send your report to the lead with the session message tool (`send_message` to session_01GUxQEgr89W9ggpA1toGhGY), at most 45 lines: the "In short" section word for word; the two counts; the five most important things you would have the founder decide first; where you disagree with something "Decided for you"; steps you propose for the plan (each one line: what, for whom, when it blocks); what you could not check; the newest commit id. Then stop.
